guide.summary: Linear documents OAuth2 authorization-code flow for applications that act for individual users, with user actor as the default. The default read scope gives read access to the authorizing user's account, which covers the confirmed read-only issue title request. Pagination uses cursor-based first/after arguments with hasNextPage. Setup requires creating an OAuth2 application with redirect URLs, plus the client ID and secret for token exchange; this is untested. Write scopes are not needed and are excluded. Distribution to other customer organizations is not established by the supplied sources, which tie directory submission to agents.

findings.title: Use user-actor OAuth2 authorization code flow per customer account
findings.detail: Linear supports OAuth2 for applications integrating with Linear. The default actor is user, meaning each user authorizes the app for their own authentication. Token exchange returns an access token valid for 24 hours plus a refresh token that must be used to renew it.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer connects their own Linear account and the app reads issues as that person.

steps.title: Read the first page of issue titles
steps.detail: Query the GraphQL API with the Bearer access token for issue ids and titles, requesting the first page with pageInfo. Expected output is an issues connection with nodes containing title values and a pageInfo object with hasNextPage and endCursor. This is a read-only query; no create, update or delete mutation is used.
steps.doneWhen: The response contains issues.nodes with title values and pageInfo.hasNextPage and endCursor fields. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: --data '{ "query": "{ issues { nodes { id title } } }" }' \
} ``` To query the next 10, simply pass the value of `pageInfo.endCursor` as `after` parameter for the next request. You can do this as long as `pageInfo.hasNextPage` return true
``` Or pass the token as an authorization header: `Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>`

request.example: curl '-X' 'POST' 'https://api.linear.app/graphql' '-H' 'Content-Type: application/json' '-H' 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>' '--data' '{"query":"query { issues(first: 10) { nodes { id title } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }"}'

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: from the token response of exchange-authorization-code
issue title is read from issues.nodes[].title in the data object

steps.title: Read the next page of issue titles using the returned cursor
steps.detail: Repeat the read query with after set to the pageInfo.endCursor returned by read-issue-titles-page-1 while pageInfo.hasNextPage is true. Stop when hasNextPage is false. Only the cursor from the prior response is used; no cursor is invented. Repeat the same read query, replacing after with the pageInfo.endCursor from the immediately previous response, until pageInfo.hasNextPage returns false. Stop condition is hasNextPage false as documented.
steps.doneWhen: Pages are requested in sequence until pageInfo.hasNextPage is false, and all returned titles are collected. The final response has pageInfo.hasNextPage set to false and no further cursor is requested. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.
